absent: Selection logic and address derivation for counter property helpers that report preemptibility and assert validity.
Full expansion and initial values for base counter zero and init helpers and spin lock init and unlocked helpers.
Underlying raw spin and real time spin acquisition and release implementations and arch locked and contended queries.
Dependency map structure and semantics of subclass handling and caller address tracking.
Analysis marking scopes and region size constants for race detection.
Concrete ordering guarantees of read and write barriers beyond placement.
Preemption and bottom half and interrupt masking effects and single versus multi processor configuration choice.
Complete usage contracts for latch versus classic counters and for scoped versus manual retry loops.

findings.text: Optimistic counter reads expose four related operations. An attempt operation reports whether sampling may start and provides the observed even value, a raw opening operation provides an even sample without waiting even when a writer is active, a checked validation operation provides ordering before comparing the opening sample with the current value, and an unchecked validation operation performs the comparison without ordering. The attempt operation is raw_seqcount_try_begin and the raw opening operation is raw_seqcount_begin and the checked validation is read_seqcount_retry and the unchecked validation is __read_seqcount_retry with helpers do___read_seqcount_retry and do_read_seqcount_retry.

Counter updates expose paired opening and closing operations plus two standalone invalidation operations. Raw opening and closing adjust the counter around a write window with ordering and conditional preemption control, nested and plain checked variants add dependency tracking with subclass selection, a barrier variant advances the counter twice with ordering to invalidate readers without holding exclusion, and an invalidate variant advances by an even step with ordering. Relevant operations are raw_write_seqcount_begin and raw_write_seqcount_end and write_seqcount_begin_nested and write_seqcount_begin and write_seqcount_end and raw_write_seqcount_barrier and write_seqcount_invalidate.

Latch counters provide a lightweight single writer mechanism with separate read sampling and single step update. Readers can sample the current value with a raw helper that relies on address dependency or with a checked helper that adds analysis marking, and can validate the sample with raw or checked retry helpers where the raw form supplies ordering. Writers advance the counter by a single step bracketed by ordering, with distinct begin and end wrappers that mark analysis scope. Related names are raw_read_seqcount_latch and read_seqcount_latch and raw_read_seqcount_latch_retry and read_seqcount_latch_retry and raw_write_seqcount_latch and write_seqcount_latch_begin and write_seqcount_latch and write_seqcount_latch_end with seqcount_latch_init for initialization.

Sequential locks combine a counter with an embedded spin lock for writer serialization. Initialization sets both the spin protection and the associated counter, a static definition helper creates a named instance in unlocked state, optimistic readers open with read_seqbegin and validate with read_seqretry, and writers serialize with write_seqlock before opening the counter window and close with write_sequnlock before releasing the spin protection. Initialization helpers are seqlock_init and DEFINE_SEQLOCK and __SEQLOCK_UNLOCKED.

Writer acquisition offers context specific variants that extend the basic pattern with bottom half or interrupt control. Each variant secures the embedded spin protection with the corresponding exclusion level before opening the counter window and reverses the order on release, with a flags saving form that returns processor state for later restore. Variants are write_seqlock_bh and write_sequnlock_bh and write_seqlock_irq and write_sequnlock_irq and __write_seqlock_irqsave and write_seqlock_irqsave and write_sequnlock_irqrestore.

Exclusive read access and adaptive fallback are provided alongside optimistic reads. Exclusive helpers acquire only the embedded spin protection in shared mode with matching release helpers for plain and bottom half and interrupt and flags saving contexts. Adaptive helpers choose between optimistic sampling and exclusive acquisition based on supplied parity, with separate completion helpers that either validate the sample or release the held protection, including a flags saving opening paired with a flags restoring completion. Adaptive names are read_seqbegin_or_lock and need_seqretry and done_seqretry and read_seqbegin_or_lock_irqsave and done_seqretry_irqrestore.

Scoped reading provides loop based retry with automatic cleanup and fallback to locking. A scoped helper initializes temporary state with an optimistic sample and iterates until completion, a next helper validates the sample and either finishes or transitions to a caller selected locked mode, and cleanup helpers release any acquired spin protection with or without flags restore. A guard constructor helper ties initialization to scope entry. Helpers are scoped_seqlock_read and __scoped_seqlock_next and __scoped_seqlock_cleanup_ctx and class_seqlock_init_constructor.

Spin protection is accessed through portable wrappers that delegate to raw or real time implementations depending on configuration. Plain and bottom half and interrupt and flags saving acquire and release operations exist in both generic and real time forms, raw forms forward to low level primitives, initialization has a debug aware form that records a class key and a simple assignment form, and query helpers report locked and contended state while a low level acquire helper combines analysis marking with arch acquisition and ordering. An after lock ordering helper is also provided.

Stability is encoded in counter parity with even meaning stable and odd meaning update in progress. Raw opening masks toward even so that a concurrent writer causes later validation to fail rather than blocking, attempt opening refuses to start when odd, and validation succeeds only when the current value still equals the opening sample. Adaptive helpers treat even input as a request for optimistic sampling and odd input as a request for exclusive acquisition.

Classic updates move the counter from even to odd on opening and from odd to the next even on closing, each step separated from protected data by ordering. A barrier update performs two steps with ordering to force reader retry without holding exclusion, an invalidate update adds an even step with ordering, and latch updates advance by a single step with ordering on both sides so that readers observe monotonic progress rather than paired windows.

Preemption control and dependency tracking are tied to counter properties. Raw and checked opening operations disable preemption only when the associated counter is marked preemptible and re enable on matching close, while checked opening records dependency acquisition with subclass and caller address and checked closing records matching release. Latch begin and end mark analysis scope without preemption changes.

Writers serialize through the embedded spin lock held across the whole counter window, opening the counter only after acquiring spin protection and closing the counter before releasing it. Optimistic readers never acquire spin protection and rely solely on sample validation with retry. Exclusive readers acquire the same spin protection in shared mode to observe without retry.

Context exclusion must pair exactly between acquisition and release. Bottom half variants require matching bottom half release, interrupt variants require matching interrupt release, and flags saving acquisition requires flags restoring release with the saved state. Real time forms differ by managing bottom half separately from spin acquisition and by leaving interrupt state and saved flags untouched, while generic forms delegate all three aspects to raw primitives.

Adaptive and scoped acquisition obey parity driven ownership. When the supplied marker is even the caller owns no lock and must validate the optimistic sample, when odd the caller owns the embedded spin protection and must release it through the matching completion helper. Scoped state records which lock if any is held so that scope exit releases exactly the acquired protection, and locked states terminate without further validation while the lockless state validates before deciding to finish or escalate.

The base counter object holds a single counter word plus optional dependency tracking that is present only when allocation debugging is enabled. The counter word is the sole field used for parity and validation, while the tracking field when present records lock dependency state for checked updates.

Associated counter variants embed the base counter plus an optional pointer to the serializing primitive. Inclusion of the pointer is controlled by a helper that either keeps or discards its argument depending on real time configuration, yielding distinct named types for raw spin and spin and read write lock and mutex associations with per variant preemptibility and base naming.

The sequential lock object pairs an associated spin counter with an embedded spin lock. Readers sample the counter portion while writers hold the spin portion across the counter window, and real time builds rely on the associated form to avoid reader starvation of writers. Static construction composes a zeroed counter tied to the embedded lock with an unlocked spin value.

The latch object is a thin wrapper holding exactly one base counter with no embedded lock. Zero construction delegates to the base counter zero helper applied to the wrapped field, and initialization delegates to the base counter init helper applied to the address of the wrapped field.

Scoped handling uses a small state enumeration and a scratch record. The enumeration distinguishes finished and plain locked and flags saving locked and lockless sampling states. The scratch record holds the current state plus a data word for sample or flags and two optional pointers identifying which plain or flags saving lock is held, both initially empty and populated only when escalation occurs.

Scoped reading starts lockless with an initial sample and iterates until finished. From lockless a successful validation finishes while a failed validation moves to a caller chosen target, acquiring plain or flags saving protection as requested or resampling for another optimistic attempt. From either locked state the next step finishes immediately, releasing through scope cleanup, and reaching finished then advancing again is treated as a defect.

Counter lifecycles differ between classic and latch use. Classic use cycles between stable even values through a transient odd value bracketed by ordering, with barrier and invalidate transitions jumping directly from one even value to the next even value to force retry. Latch use advances monotonically by single steps with ordering before and after each step, and readers accept any stable observation with retry decided by equality against the opening sample.

Optimistic seqlock reading is entered through an opening operation annotated as shared acquisition and exited through a validation operation annotated as shared release. The opening operation delegates to counter begin on the embedded associated counter and the validation delegates to counter retry with the opening sample, requiring callers to repeat protected loads when validation reports failure.

Seqlock writing is entered through acquisition helpers annotated as exclusive acquisition and exited through matching release helpers annotated as exclusive release. Entry secures the embedded spin protection with the requested context level then opens the counter window, while exit closes the counter window then releases the spin protection with the matching context level, with flags forms threading saved processor state from entry to exit.

Low level spin acquisition marks analysis ownership then acquires the architecture specific ticket and applies ordering for memory mapped input output. Portable wrappers select between raw delegation and real time blocking acquisition, with plain forms forwarding directly and context forms adding bottom half or interrupt handling around the core acquisition.

Raw opening without stabilization must be confined to small hot paths with high external likelihood of success because it defers contention detection to validation time and saves only a single branch. Attempt opening should be preferred when stabilization cost resembles lock cost and a slow path can take the lock, since it avoids speculation entirely when the counter is odd.

Ordering must not be omitted inadvertently. Unchecked validation provides no read ordering so callers must supply equivalent ordering before consuming protected data and document how it is provided, and raw latch sampling omits a full barrier in reliance on address dependency pairing with the first writer ordering point, with retry supplying the missing ordering.

Configuration specific simplifications change guarantees. Single processor arch acquisition may reduce to a plain store with compiler ordering or to a pure compiler barrier with no atomicity, real time flags handling may clear and ignore saved state, real time interrupt handling may perform no masking, and contended queries may unconditionally report idle when architecture support is absent. Callers must not rely on masking or contention signals where these simplifications apply.

Slow path lock code is segregated into a dedicated subsection whose name combines a fixed textual prefix with the compilation unit name, with helpers to open the subsection and emit the label once and to return to the previous section, plus an attribute directing lock functions into spinlock text.

Header inclusion is guarded by dedicated preprocessor symbols for sequence lock types and for spin locks with an inner guard distinguishing nested inclusion, and raw lock initialization records a spin wait classification when dependency tracking is present while contended queries without architecture support evaluate to idle.
